_why: The archive's own folds, written rather than derived. namefold.py refuses to fold a
cluster that changes a LETTER rather than an accent, because that is a claim about a
family and not a spelling rule. These are the claims this archive has read and made.
FERNANDES -> FERNANDEZ, decided 20 September 2026 on three pieces of evidence:
1. THE APEX ACT ITSELF USES THE S. The marginal heading of Sancho Llerena's marriage
of 8 January 1791 at Canelones - DGS 8166578 image 2687, the single document this
archive spent weeks finding - reads 'Sancho Llerena, y Maria FERNANDES. Casados y
Velados'. The woman this register writes Maria Fernandez throughout is written
Fernandes by the clerk who married her.
2. THE OTHER TWO SIT BESIDE GONSALES AND ALBARES. In the 1825 San Jose marriage of
Alejandro Lerena the same hand writes 'MARIA JOSSEFA GONSALES', 'MARGARITA
FERNANDES ALBARES' and 'JUAN FERNANDES ALVARES'. A clerk writing s for z in every
surname on the page is a habit, not four different families.
3. IT IS FOUR TOKENS AGAINST 344. Nothing in this register depends on the S spelling
being a separate line, and the two documents that carry it are both about people
already held under the Z.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM: that every Fernandes anywhere is a Fernandez. Portuguese
Fernandes is a real and distinct surname, and the Banda Oriental had Portuguese in it.
This fold is about THIS corpus, where the four instances are all demonstrably the
s/z habit of two Spanish-language clerks.
GONZALES and GONSALES -> GONZALEZ, decided the same day and on the same reasoning.
Every instance in this corpus is ONE WOMAN: MARIA (JOSEFA) GONZALEZ, mother of
Mauricio Lerena, named as the groom's mother on the San Jose marriages of 16 September
1825 and 3 February 1837. The 1825 act is the one that also writes FERNANDES, ALBARES
and ALVARES - the same hand, the same s-for-z. This archive's own notes already give
her the fuller MARIA JOSEFA GONZALEZ; the indexes give Gonzales and Gonsales.
NOT FOLDED, and deliberately: the FORENAME question. Whether she is Maria or Maria
Josefa is unreconciled on an image and both forms are kept. This decision is about the
SURNAME's s/z only.
